_doc: Plain-English descriptions for the Lending Radar card, sections 1 and 2. DESCRIPTIVE ONLY: no figures allowed here (tests reject digits). Direct industries use engine/credit_lens.json; this file covers the proxy industries and sourced local cluster facts. Any local figure must carry a source URL and a date.

what.dairy_products: Dairies collect milk from farmers and sell packaged milk, curd, ghee, butter and cheese.
what.seafood_processing: Plants buy shrimp and fish from farms and boats, then freeze, pack and export them.
what.meat_poultry_processing: Units slaughter, cut, chill and pack meat and chicken for shops, hotels and export.
what.bakery_confectionery: Bakeries and factories make bread, biscuits, cakes and sweets and sell through distributors and shops.
what.flour_dal_mills: Mills grind wheat into flour and clean, split and polish pulses into dal for traders and brands.
what.snacks_namkeen: Units fry and pack namkeen, chips and snacks for local shops and branded distribution.
what.animal_feed: Plants mix maize, soymeal and other grains into feed for poultry farms and dairy cattle.
what.distilleries_ethanol: Distilleries turn molasses or grain into alcohol for liquor makers and ethanol for oil companies.
what.soft_drinks_water: Bottlers fill soft drinks and packaged water in plastic bottles for shops and distributors.
what.bidi_making: Contractors and home workers roll tobacco in tendu leaves into bidis for brand owners.
what.cotton_ginning: Ginners buy raw cotton (kapas) from farmers, separate seed from fibre and sell bales to spinning mills.
what.handloom_powerloom: Small weavers turn cotton or blended yarn into grey cloth on handlooms or powerlooms, often as job-work.
what.silk_weaving: Weavers turn silk yarn into sarees and fabric, mostly sold through traders around wedding seasons.
what.woollen_textiles: Units spin and weave wool into shawls, blankets and knitwear, with sales peaking in winter.
what.textile_processing: Process houses dye, print and finish grey fabric for traders and weavers, usually on job-work charges.
what.technical_textiles: Units make nonwovens, coated fabrics, bags and industrial fabrics from polymers for institutional buyers.
what.home_textiles: Mills make towels, bedsheets and curtains, much of it for large US and European retailers.
what.hosiery_knitwear: Units knit yarn into vests, innerwear, socks and sweaters and sell through dealers.
what.footwear: Factories make shoes and sandals from leather, rubber and synthetics for brands, retailers and export.
what.leather_tanning: Tanneries treat raw hides and skins into finished leather for shoe and leather-goods makers.
what.leather_goods: Units cut and stitch finished leather into bags, belts, wallets and gloves, mainly for export buyers.
what.plywood_laminates: Units peel and press timber into plywood, veneer and laminates for furniture makers and builders.
what.sawmills_timber: Sawmills cut imported and local logs into timber for construction, packaging and furniture.
what.packaging_corrugated: Units turn kraft paper into corrugated boxes and cartons for consumer-goods and e-commerce shippers.
what.printing_publishing: Presses print books, labels, cartons and stationery for publishers and packaging buyers.
what.lubricants: Blenders mix base oil and additives into engine and industrial oils for workshops and factories.
what.agrochemicals: Plants make and pack pesticides and weedkillers sold to farmers through dealers.
what.paints_coatings: Factories mix resins, pigments and solvents into paints for homes, industry and vehicles.
what.soaps_cosmetics: Units make soaps, detergents and personal-care products and sell through distributors.
what.specialty_chemicals: Plants make small-volume, high-value chemicals for pharma, agrochemical and industrial buyers.
what.industrial_gases: Plants separate and bottle oxygen, nitrogen and other gases for steel works, factories and hospitals.
what.fireworks_matches: Units make crackers and safety matches, with most sales packed around Diwali.
what.manmade_fibres: Plants turn PTA and MEG (crude-oil derivatives) or wood pulp into polyester and viscose fibre and yarn.
what.api_bulk_drugs: Plants make the active ingredients of medicines and sell them to formulation makers in India and abroad.
what.formulations: Plants turn active ingredients into tablets, capsules and injections for Indian and export markets.
what.ayush_herbal: Units process herbs into Ayurvedic and herbal medicines and personal-care products.
what.medical_devices: Units make syringes, implants, diagnostic kits and equipment for hospitals and distributors.
what.rubber_tyres: Factories turn natural and synthetic rubber into tyres, tubes and rubber parts for vehicle makers and replacement buyers.
what.plastic_packaging: Units turn polymer granules into films, pouches, bottles and containers for packaged-goods companies.
what.pvc_pipes: Units extrude PVC resin into pipes and fittings for housing, plumbing and farm irrigation.
what.bricks_kilns: Kilns mould and fire clay into bricks for local construction, mostly in the dry season.
what.stone_granite: Units cut and polish granite, marble and stone slabs for builders and export.
what.refractories: Plants make heat-resistant bricks and linings for steel, cement and glass furnaces.
what.steel_rerolling: Re-rollers heat steel billets and scrap and roll them into TMT bars and sections for construction.
what.sponge_iron: Plants reduce iron ore with coal into sponge iron, and smelt ferro alloys for steel makers.
what.aluminium_products: Units roll, extrude and cast aluminium into sheets, sections and parts.
what.castings_forgings: Foundries and forges shape molten or heated metal into parts for vehicles, tractors and machinery.
what.fasteners_hardware: Units make bolts, nuts, screws and hardware from steel wire rod for industry and export.
what.steel_utensils: Units press and polish stainless steel into kitchen utensils sold through dealers.
what.hand_tools: Units forge and grind steel into spanners, pliers and cutting tools, much of it for export.
what.electronic_components: Units make and assemble circuit boards and parts for electronics brands and assemblers.
what.mobile_assembly: Plants assemble phones, televisions and gadgets from imported and local parts for brand owners.
what.solar_modules: Plants assemble solar cells into panels for power developers and rooftop installers.
what.cables_wires: Units draw copper and aluminium into wires and cables for builders, utilities and industry.
what.transformers_switchgear: Units build transformers, switchgear and panels, mostly for power utilities and projects.
what.lighting_led: Units assemble LED lamps and fittings, often from imported parts, for dealers and projects.
what.appliances_fans: Factories make fans, coolers and home appliances and sell through dealers, with seasonal peaks.
what.batteries: Units make lead-acid and lithium batteries for vehicles, inverters and replacement buyers.
what.pumps_valves: Units make pumps, motors and valves for farms, buildings and industry, in India and abroad.
what.machine_tools: Units build lathes, machining centres and presses bought by auto and engineering factories.
what.textile_machinery: Units make looms, embroidery and processing machines for textile mills and weavers.
what.tractors_agri_machinery: Makers and dealers build and sell tractors and farm equipment to farmers.
what.diesel_engines: Units make diesel engines and generator sets for farms, buildings and project sites.
what.vehicle_oem: Plants assemble cars, trucks and buses and sell them through dealers.
what.ev_components: Units make electric vehicles and their batteries, motors and controllers.
what.two_wheelers: Plants make scooters and motorcycles sold through dealers, with a large rural customer base.
what.bicycles: Units make bicycles and parts for dealers, exporters and government schemes.
what.shipbuilding: Yards build and repair ships and boats against long, milestone-paid contracts.
what.railway_wagons: Units build wagons, coaches and parts mainly against Indian Railways orders.
what.defence_aerospace: Units make parts and systems for defence and aircraft makers on long contracts.
what.wooden_furniture: Units make wooden and modular furniture for homes, offices and export buyers.
what.gold_jewellery: Workshops turn gold into jewellery for retailers and wholesalers, with wedding-season peaks.
what.imitation_jewellery: Units make fashion jewellery from brass and alloys for traders and festival demand.
what.sports_goods: Units make cricket bats, balls and sports gear from leather, willow and synthetics, much of it for export.
what.toys: Units make plastic, wooden and electronic toys that compete with imports.
what.coir_products: Units turn coconut husk fibre into mats, ropes and geotextiles, largely for export.
what.jute_mills: Mills spin raw jute into sacking and bags, largely for government grain packing.
what.dairy_farming: Farms keep cattle and buffaloes and sell milk to dairies and cooperatives.
what.poultry_farming: Farms raise broiler chickens and layers for meat and eggs, often under contract with integrators.
what.fisheries_aquaculture: Farmers and boat owners raise shrimp and fish in ponds or catch them at sea for processors.
what.horticulture: Growers raise fruit, vegetables and flowers for mandis, processors and export.
what.plantation_rubber: Estates and smallholders grow rubber and other plantation crops for processors.
what.seeds: Companies breed, grow and pack seeds and sell them to farmers through dealers.
what.sericulture: Farmers grow mulberry and rear silkworms to sell cocoons to silk reelers.
what.cold_storage: Warehouses store potatoes, fruit and other produce at low temperature for a rental.
what.coal_mining: Mines and washeries extract and clean coal, mostly for power plants and industry.
what.quarrying_sand: Quarries crush stone and dig sand and aggregates for construction.
what.iron_ore_mining: Mines extract iron ore for steel plants and export under government leases.
what.residential_real_estate: Developers buy land, build homes and sell flats, often before completion.
what.solar_epc: Contractors design and install solar plants and rooftop systems for developers, firms and homes.
what.water_sanitation: Contractors build water-supply, sewage and sanitation projects, mostly for government bodies.
what.oil_gas_pipelines: Companies lay and run gas pipelines and city gas networks, earning tariffs and connection fees.
what.civil_contractors: Contractors build roads, buildings and public works and are paid against running bills.
what.logistics_warehousing: Operators run warehouses, transport and delivery networks for manufacturers and e-commerce.
what.trucking_fleet: Owners run trucks that carry goods for traders and factories, paid per trip or per tonne.
what.restaurants_cafes: Restaurants, cafes and caterers serve food, usually from rented premises.
what.it_bpo: Firms run back-office, call-centre and IT-enabled services for clients in India and abroad.
what.hospitals_healthcare: Hospitals, clinics and diagnostic labs treat patients and are paid by patients, insurers and government schemes.
what.education_institutions: Schools, colleges and coaching centres earn fees from students.
what.media_entertainment: Firms run cinemas, channels, studios and events that earn from tickets and advertising.
what.microfinance: Lenders give small group loans to low-income borrowers, usually women, repaid in small instalments.
what.textile_trading: Traders buy fabric from weavers and processors and sell it on credit to wholesalers and garment makers.
what.diamond_trading: Traders buy and sell rough and polished diamonds and jewellery, often extending credit to buyers abroad.
what.agri_commodity_trading: Traders buy grain, pulses and other crops at mandis and sell them to processors and exporters.
what.steel_trading: Traders stock steel from mills and sell it to builders and fabricators, often on credit.
what.pharma_distribution: Distributors stock medicines from makers and supply chemists and hospitals on credit.
what.fmcg_distribution: Distributors stock packaged goods from brands and supply local shops on credit.
what.auto_dealerships: Dealers buy vehicles from manufacturers and sell them with service, spares and loans.
what.jewellery_retail: Shops sell gold and diamond jewellery, holding large stocks of metal.
what.electronics_retail: Shops sell phones, appliances and gadgets from many brands.
what.ecommerce_sellers: Sellers list goods on online marketplaces and are paid after delivery and returns.
what.fuel_stations: Dealers sell petrol and diesel for an oil company at a fixed dealer margin.
what.job_work_units: Small units process material owned by a larger firm and earn a job-work charge.
what.fabrication_workshops: Workshops cut, weld and machine steel parts and structures for larger firms.
what.tailoring_units: Small units stitch garments for traders, shops and local customers.
what.small_food_units: Small units make bakery items, sweets and snacks for local shops.

what.t: Polyester yarn, made from crude-oil derivatives, is woven into grey fabric on powerlooms, often as job-work, then dyed, printed, embroidered and finished for dress-material traders and garment buyers.
Surat makes about 65% of India's synthetic textiles, with yearly sales of about Rs 85,000 crore (as cited by the Southern Gujarat Chamber of Commerce and Industry).

money.t: The margin is in processing and finishing; grey fabric is a commodity. Pure job-work units earn only a conversion charge and have no pricing power.
Yarn and power decide the margin. Yarn follows crude oil, so a unit must pass price rises on quickly or absorb them.

checks: Power bills against the shift register, every month: falling machine hours mean a slowdown.
Yarn purchase register against the stock statement, every month: yarn piling up while sales stay flat means the unit is funding inventory instead of selling.
Wage, EPF (Employees' Provident Fund) and ESI (Employees' State Insurance) payments on time: late payments are an early sign of stress or a strike.
Any FIR or labour department notice against the unit.
